chunks: From him, from al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb, from Sayf ibn ʿUmayrah, from Ibn Bukayr, who said:

I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about an owned slave who falsely accuses a free man of fornication. He said: “He is flogged eighty lashes. This is from the rights of the people. But as for what is from the rights of Allah, then he is struck with half of the hadd.” I said: What is that in which half of the hadd is administered? He said: “If he commits zina or drinks wine, then this is from the rights of Allah in which half of the hadd is administered.”

key_terms.حُقُوقِ اللَّهِ: rights belonging to Allah in the legal sense
key_terms.حُقُوقِ النَّاسِ: rights belonging to human beings that are legally enforceable
key_terms.نِصْفَ الْحَدِّ: half of the prescribed legal punishment

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a slave who commits qadhf, zina, or drinks wine in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith distinguishes between the legal consequences of offenses involving the rights of people and offenses involving the rights of Allah for an enslaved person. It states that false accusation against a free person carries the full hadd of eighty lashes, while certain offenses categorized as the rights of Allah, such as zina and drinking wine, entail half of the hadd.
